articles.text:
ASURVEY of 177 of the country's top neurosurgeons, neumlogists and critical care specialists shows that over half (59.2 per cent) were not trained in medical colleges to certify brain death - aknowledge gap thatimpacts organ donations, according toa study published recently by doctors at the All India Institute of Medical Science (AIIMS), Delhi. While nearly three-fourth (74.5%) of the doctors surveyed worked at teaching hospitals, only 10 per cent said they regularly trained their residents in brain death certification. DESPITE INDIA performing among the highest number of organ transplants in the world, the national organ donation rate has hovered under one per million population for years, compared with more than 30 per million in countries suchas Spain. Experts point out that better awareness, stronger hospital systems and streamlined brain death certification are critical to bridging this gap.
